messages.subject: Choosing the right truncation distance
parts:
Hi,
I am Aditya, an analyst in Nature Conservation Foundation, India. I am completely new to distance sampling  and I have been using the Distance package in R for analyzing line transect data of prey species for leopards in the Western Ghats. I have been able to run the codes without any problem but I had a question regarding choosing the truncation distance. I have two study regions. In region 1, I have no detection beyond 80m (2 outliers beyond 200m). In region 2, I have no detection after 60m (1 outlier beyond 100 m). I have chosen to run the models setting truncation distance at 80m (using both the regions together in one model with region label as stratum, and also individually for each region). I have had no issues with running the models but I had some conceptual doubts regarding the choice of truncation distances.
My questions are:
1. Is it appropriate to choose 80m, given there is barely any detection after 60m for region2?
2. I can choose 60m as the truncation distance, in which case I only have slight variation in my abundance and density estimates. Given that these are pretty close it is fine but what about cases where there maybe a larger discrepancy between the detection distances in two regions? What would you advice for choosing a reasonable truncation distance in such cases?
3. Is there anyway to plot the detection functions (when I have region as a stratum) with individually color coded points/lines for the two regions? I could not find anything about it for the Distance package.
 
Thank you.
Aditya

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Choosing the right truncation distance
parts:
Regarding truncation Aditya, consult the last slide in the detection function lecture in our online workshop materials
https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/lecturepdfs/Ch1/L1-4%20Choosing%20a%20Detection%20Function.pdf
for a discussion of this topic.  In practice, the choice of truncation distance has little effect upon your estimates, as you have noted. The slide I indicated provides a suggestion that the truncation distance "w" be chosen such that g(w)=0.15 for a simple detection function.

Regarding your plotting question, there is a function in the Distance package called add_df_covar_line()​. There is an example of its use on our case study page

http://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-spec-covar/species-covariate-distill.html
Covariate modeling with rare species
Use of covariate to model detectability in multi-species surveys.
examples.distancesampling.org

where we have used different species as the strata and fitted a detection function using strata as a covariate:
